key_insight: Foundation interatomic potentials capture metallic-glass disorder most reliably when pre-training includes liquid and amorphous configurations, with target-specific fine-tuning offering only modest gains.
engineering_relevance: These models can reduce reliance on composition-specific potentials for simulating metallic-glass structure and properties at near first-principles accuracy.
method: Benchmark MACE foundation models against EAM during Cu–Zr–Al molecular dynamics quenches.
Validate against DFT and experiment at Cu46Zr46Al8 and across the ternary’s good glass-forming region.
Test fine-tuning on surrogate-generated glass structures and ASSYST-generated small periodic cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that OMAT-pretrained models transfer across compositions and outperform EAM, while assessing structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical, and thermal properties.
watch_item: Validate disorder and dynamics before deployment: specialization on small crystalline cells degraded performance, and transfer beyond Cu–Zr–Al is not established here.
paper_title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
